However, this Operation Fist is actually a sequel to Operation Breakthrough, and you asked me whether it was correct that the territory of mid-Podrinje was compact and under Muslim control from the village of Kamenica, that is to say, near Zvornik, all the way to Zepa, Zepa included. That is correct too. However, this sheet of paper in front of us is analysis of combat operations carried out within operation under the code-name of Pesnica, and I spoke about what Pesnica meant a moment ago, fist, a blow with a fist. And what he says here is up until the 10th of January, 1993. However, he forgot that on the 16th of January, 1993, Naser Oric carried out a counter-attack, a smaller counter-attack against Skelani and that in this way he threw out about 20.000 inhabits of Skelani. Somewhere in here I saw that he was issuing a task to a battalion from the 1st Krajina Corps. I had to bring in two battalions from the Krajina Corps to resolve the problem of Skelani and the problem was resolved on the 23rd of January. So Zivanovic is, well, carrying out a bit of an analysis here but he did not abide by the time when it's supposed to begin and when it's supposed to end. Four days beforehand he had lost the entire territory of the municipality of Skelani --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We'll have a look at another document about that. Look at the last paragraph down here. The main task of units in Operation Pesnica was to cut the Muslims forces area of concentration and to separate the Srebrenica area from the area of Cerska and liberate the Milici-Konjevic Polje-Zvornik road and so on and so forth. Do you see that paragraph? And can we have the next page now once you've read this, that is. So to cut this area, this space, where 15.000 fighters of Oric's were attacking our villages, our areas; right?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this. Actually, this is implementation of a task that he had received from the Main Staff. I think it was dated the 7th of December, one of these supplements to the directives issued. Until then we had communication or we had a corridor along the following route: Vlasenica-Sekovici-Caparde-Zvornik. And we made this corridor in the following way. We cut down a forest by this road between Sekovici and Caparde. You remember that, 1 kilometre on the left and 1 kilometre on the right, and for years those logs were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but can I just ask for the next page. In other words, let us tell the Trial Chamber that this was a longer route and that it went around the territory?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I think that it had to do with this last supplement dated the 4th of December. So the corridor should be Vlasenica-Milici-Zvornik, and he should do that and he is doing it through this operation entitled Pesnica, Fist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Last paragraph, take a look at that now -- no, first paragraph. It says the combat operations were co-ordinated by Miladin Prstojevic and the others, so he is still being appointed co-ordinator, in spite of his courage to change things. Take a look at this -- actually, do you agree with what I said just now, that at the time he was still the leading operations officer out there?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once again, I repeat, Colonel Prstojevic was a man who knew how to work in a high command, but he also knew how to mingle with combatants and he knew how to motivate people by his very presence. Although Zivanovic persecuted him in a way. On the other hand, he could hardly do without him. After that, Milosevic came in as his operations officer, again a literate man who could bear the command of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And look at the last paragraph. It says the successful conduct of this operation has particularly high significance for the general territory of the town of Bratunac as well as the prevention of a further relocation of the population from the general Bratunac sector to the FRY over the Drina River. So that is part of that municipality, but they were in favour of crossing the Drina River, right, and fleeing in that way?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire area to the south of Zvornik, all the way up to Zepa, Zepa included, was always ready to swim across the Drina River, which bothered us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that there is nothing bad here as regards civilians and that this is a legitimate operation with military justification?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although it is a leading question, I am going to answer with a yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted and you decide how long we're going to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not dated nor was it signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't object to it, Your Honour. I honestly did not notice that there was no date, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2137, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for today -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: If there is possibility to continue, we -- the Defence would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: If we can continue, the Defence would not oppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that it's not possible. Before we adjourn, the Chamber will issue an oral ruling on a matter which arose during the testimony of Mr. Robert Block. On the 21st of February, 2012, the accused's legal advisor orally requested that the Chamber order Witness Robert Block to look for the notes he may have taken regarding his meeting with Mr. Zoran Petrovic, or Pirocanac, on the 18th of July, 1995, and to turn them over to the accused. The accused's legal advisor argued, inter alia, that the lack of any reference to the accused in Block's notes could go directly to the accused's responsibility. The Chamber notes Mr. Block's statement during his testimony that he did not believe he took notes on those days. In any event, during his testimony, the witness did not mention that he used notes of any kind to refresh his memory before testifying in these proceedings. Given these circumstances, the Chamber thus denies the motion. We'll resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 1st day of March, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.03 p.m.,
